top_choice_rationale: P002 (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) is the best-evidenced and most mature achievement on the slate: induced proximity through a ternary complex is a physical-chemical principle with measurable cooperativity, geometry and kinetics, confirmed independently for two decades. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the designed degrader; Handa's cereblon identification explains how a small molecule reshapes an E3 ligase surface, and that mechanism underlies approved glue-class drugs, which answers my maturity concern even though no heterobifunctional degrader is approved. One citation worded around ligase recruitment covers both arms. P001 (Ciulli as third name) is a close second since the topic is the same and only the credit judgement differs; P003 and P004 add base editing, which sits next to the 2020 CRISPR prize with a short clinical record, and P004 also relies on Pd C-N coupling, which is arguably an extension of the 2010 prize. No award is ranked last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my cytochrome c oxidase work on proton and electron transfer is close to B025, which is not on the slate, and I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, which is not relevant to any proposal
